items.title: Albert Artigues Sr. Interview, 1961-12-15
items.q: The interviewee explains that 'mule' is a slang term for not paying the band, not a person. 'Nine out of ten the band got mule... Yeah, put the mule on them, wouldn't pay them, you know.'

ctx.x: you ever touched a horn? Oh yeah, I heard quite a few Dixieland bands. In those days they had all these good colored bands around town. Chris Kelly, Punch, Rene, Papa Celestine, they were all young comers then, you know what I mean? And they all played a powerful lot of music. Buddy Petit played nice stuff those days. Punch, Sam Morgan, Chris Kelly. Oh and they had quite a few good white bands. Pansaline had a good white Dixieland band. Johnny Beisdorff was at his peak. He was playing the Tokyo Gardens out at the…
What is this, Mule? What is this, Mule?

What is this, Mule? What is this? Mule? What is this? Mule? What would they have at these parties? Well they'd have a beer, whiskey, stuff to drink, and a band. Nine out of ten the band got mule, because those people didn't have a lot of money those days. They'd hire a band for around eighteen dollars. And Kid Punch would come out there and they'd get Punch or Rene or whoever was playing good and loaded. They'd come for time to pay the band off, whoever drew the party was hard to find.
